literature.headline_zh: 诺如病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期诺如病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 该倡议导致硝唑尼特使用量减少了84.4%,并实现了显著的成本节约,而不会影响患者护理或增加医院内感染率。 [10.1017/ice.2026.10605]
该平台表现出高分析灵敏度和特异性,在生菜和菠菜组织中分别实现了每100毫克1000和5000个病毒拷贝的检测限。整个检测过程大约需要2小时完成。 [10.1021/acssensors.6c03711]
2026-11-05发表的《2011年至2025年中国昆明市其他传染病性腹泻的时空动态及病原谱分析》进入本期重点文献清单，详细证据见下方单篇解读。 [10.1186/s12982-026-03177-2]

key_findings_en: The initiative resulted in an 84.4% reduction in nitazoxanide utilization and substantial cost savings without compromising patient care or increasing nosocomial infection rates. [10.1017/ice.2026.10605]

The platform exhibited high analytical sensitivity and specificity, achieving detection limits of 1000 and 5000 viral copies per 100 mg of romaine lettuce and spinach tissue, respectively. The entire assay was completed in approximately 2 hours. [10.1021/acssensors.6c03711]

From 2011 to 2025, Kunming reported 152,090 OID cases, with a mean annual incidence of 134.3 per 100,000 population (range: 62.7-273.2 per 100,000). Incidence increased significantly over the surveillance period (AAPC = 11.2%, 95% CI 3.5 to 19.3), showing a marked acceleration after 2023. [10.1186/s12982-026-03177-2]

news.headline_zh: 诺如病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期诺如病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: FDA批准了更新的bioMérieux胃肠病原体检测面板,采用重新设计的诺如病毒检测方法,如Clinical Lab Products所报道。 [news-ab473ddd87699487]
过去 30 年来,诺如病毒 被确认为邮轮 暴发 的主要原因,尽管其他病原体正在增加其贡献。此信息由 CIDRAP 报告。 [news-bf9887c83957e461]
在两周内,多个诺如病毒 暴发导致超过270人患病,患病员工继续工作加剧了病毒的传播。 [news-d4e142118005adfd]
bioMérieux宣布BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI1.1面板和GI1.1面板Mid获得FDA 510(k)清关,其中包括重新设计的诺如病毒 GI/GII检测和改进的空肠弯曲菌检测。这些面板分别旨在从单个粪便样本中检测22种和11种肠道病原体。 [news-f8a1bfda99c80eb8]
FDA批准了更新的bioMérieux GI面板的510(k)清关,其中包括重新设计的诺如病毒 GI/GII检测方法。这些面板旨在提高对胃肠感染的诊断特异性。 [news-60aa8044a27c2e48]

news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Norovirus news developments.
key_findings_en: The FDA cleared an updated bioMérieux GI Panels with a redesigned Norovirus assay, as reported by Clinical Lab Products. [news-ab473ddd87699487]
Norovirus is identified as the primary cause of cruise ship outbreaks over the past 30 years, though other pathogens are increasingly contributing. This is reported by CIDRAP. [news-bf9887c83957e461]
Multiple norovirus outbreaks sickened more than 270 people over two weeks, with ill staff continuing to work contributing to the spread of the virus. [news-d4e142118005adfd]

bioMérieux announced the FDA 510(k) clearance for the BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI1.1 Panel and GI1.1 Panel Mid, which include a redesigned norovirus GI/GII assay and improved Campylobacter detection. These panels are designed to detect 22 and 11 gastrointestinal pathogens, respectively, from a single stool sample. [news-f8a1bfda99c80eb8]

The FDA granted 510(k) clearance for the updated bioMérieux GI Panels, which include a redesigned Norovirus GI/GII assay. The panels are intended to improve diagnostic specificity for gastrointestinal infections. [news-60aa8044a27c2e48]

The FDA cleared an updated bioMérieux GI Panels with a redesigned Norovirus assay, as reported by Clinical Lab Products. [news-ab473ddd87699487]. Norovirus is identified as the primary cause of cruise ship outbreaks over the past 30 years, though other pathogens are increasingly contributing. This is reported by CIDRAP. [news-bf9887c83957e461]. Multiple norovirus outbreaks sickened more than 270 people over two weeks, with ill staff continuing to work contributing to the spread of the virus. [news-d4e142118005adfd]. bioMérieux announced the FDA 510(k) clearance for the BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI1.1 Panel and GI1.1 Panel Mid, which include a redesigned norovirus GI/GII assay and improved Campylobacter detection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of data on nitazoxanide utilization in patients with cancer and the risk of norovirus infection for both patients and healthcare workers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A quality improvement initiative was conducted in a hospital setting to evaluate the impact of diagnostic stewardship on nitazoxanide utilization in patients with cancer who were suspected of having norovirus infection.
analysis.methods: The study utilized a multiplex polymerase chain reaction platform for norovirus detection, which may yield false-positive results, and implemented a diagnostic stewardship program to monitor and adjust nitazoxanide use.
analysis.main_results: The initiative resulted in an 84.4% reduction in nitazoxanide utilization and substantial cost savings without compromising patient care or increasing nosocomial infection rates.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that diagnostic stewardship can effectively reduce unnecessary nitazoxanide use in cancer patients while maintaining clinical outcomes and preventing infections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeted diagnostic strategies can improve resource allocation and reduce costs in the management of norovirus infections in immunocompromised patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a single institution and the potential for false-positive results with the multiplex polymerase chain reaction platform, but the evidence is strong due to the clear reduction in nitazoxanide use and cost savings.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated a diagnostic stewardship initiative aimed at improving the diagnosis of norovirus and reducing the utilization of nitazoxanide in patients with cancer. The initiative was implemented in a hospital setting and involved the use of a multiplex polymerase chain reaction platform for norovirus detection. The results showed an 84.4% reduction in nitazoxanide use and significant cost savings without compromising patient care or increasing nosocomial infections. The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that diagnostic stewardship can effectively reduce unnecessary medication use in cancer patients while maintaining clinical outcomes. The study's implications suggest that targeted diagnostic strategies may enhance resource allocation and reduce costs in managing norovirus infections in immunocompromised individuals. However, the study's limitations include its focus on a single institution and the potential for false-positive results with the polymerase chain reaction platform, which may affect the generalizability of the findings.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and pathogen spectrum of other infectious diarrhea in Kunming, China from 2011 to 2025
papers.abstract: Other infectious diarrhea (OID) is one of the most frequently reported notifiable infectious diseases in China. As the capital of Yunnan Province, Kunming serves as an important regional hub in Southwest China and a gateway to the Greater Mekong Subregion. Its patterns of regional population mobility and local disease transmission are complex and region-specific, making Kunming an informative setting for sentinel surveillance and epidemiological investigations. This study investigated the long-term epidemiological characteristics and pathogen spectrum changes of OID in Kunming from 2011 to 2025. Temporal, spatial, demographic and pathogen-related patterns were assessed using descriptive epidemiological analyses, time-series and trend analyses. Seasonal-trend decomposition using Loess (STL) was utilized to characterize long-term temporal trends and seasonal patterns of OID. Continuous wavelet transform was applied to identify periodic fluctuations and temporal changes in epidemic patterns. The Shannon-Wiener diversity index was used to evaluate changes in pathogen diversity. Joinpoint regression was performed to assess long-term incidence trends across different population groups. From 2011 to 2025, Kunming reported 152,090 OID cases, with a mean annual incidence of 134.3 per 100,000 population (range: 62.7-273.2 per 100,000). Incidence increased significantly over the surveillance period (AAPC = 11.2%, 95% CI 3.5 to 19.3), showing a marked acceleration after 2023. OID cases occurred across all age groups, with those aged 0-4 years accounting for the largest proportion (67.0%, 101,899/152,090), while incidence increased across all age groups (all P < 0.001). Among 38,902 laboratory-confirmed cases, viral infections predominated (99.2%). Rotavirus remained the most prevalent pathogen (69.7%), followed by norovirus (26.7%). Both were mainly concentrated among children aged 0-4 years (89.1% and 72.0%, respectively). Spatially, OID incidence varied across counties and districts, with increasingly synchronized regional increases observed in recent years, particularly after 2024. Our findings from routinely collected surveillance data indicate that OID epidemiology in Kunming has shifted from traditional epidemic fluctuations toward broader structural changes, characterized by expanding affected populations, evolving pathogen composition, and changing spatial epidemic patterns. Although the observed changes in pathogen composition may have been influenced by testing practices, the findings highlight increasing epidemiological complexity and emerging control challenges. Accordingly, prevention strategies should integrate population diversity, spatial differences, and pathogen composition.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the long-term epidemiological characteristics and pathogen spectrum changes of other infectious diarrhea (OID) in Kunming, China, from 2011 to 2025, as OID is one of the most frequently reported notifiable infectious diseases in China.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Kunming, China, from 2011 to 2025, focusing on OID cases across all age groups, with a particular emphasis on children aged 0-4 years. It included 152,090 OID cases reported during the surveillance period.
analysis.methods: Temporal, spatial, demographic and pathogen-related patterns were assessed using descriptive epidemiological analyses, time-series and trend analyses. Joinpoint regression was performed to assess long-term incidence trends across different population groups. Seasonal-trend decomposition using Loess (STL) and continuous wavelet transform were applied to identify periodic fluctuations and temporal changes in epidemic patterns. The Shannon-Wiener diversity index was used to evaluate changes in pathogen diversity.
analysis.main_results: From 2011 to 2025, Kunming reported 152,090 OID cases, with a mean annual incidence of 134.3 per 100,000 population (range: 62.7-273.2 per 100,000). Incidence increased significantly over the surveillance period (AAPC = 11.2%, 95% CI 3.5 to 19.3), showing a marked acceleration after 2023. OID cases occurred across all age groups, with those aged 0-4 years accounting for the largest proportion (67.0%, 101,899/152,090), while incidence increased across all age groups (all P < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that OID epidemiology in Kunming has shifted from traditional epidemic fluctuations toward broader structural changes, characterized by expanding affected populations, evolving pathogen composition, and changing spatial epidemic patterns.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the increasing epidemiological complexity of OID and the need for prevention strategies that integrate population diversity, spatial differences, and pathogen composition to address emerging control challenges.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The observed changes in pathogen composition may have been influenced by testing practices, which limits the confidence in the findings. However, the study provides a comprehensive analysis of OID trends and patterns, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the spatiotemporal dynamics and pathogen spectrum of other infectious diarrhea (OID) in Kunming, China, from 2011 to 2025. It highlights the increasing incidence of OID, particularly among children aged 0-4 years, and identifies rotavirus and norovirus as the most prevalent pathogens. The research underscores the need for integrated prevention strategies due to the evolving epidemiological patterns. However, the study acknowledges potential limitations from testing practices, which may affect the interpretation of pathogen composition changes. The findings contribute to understanding the structural shifts in OID epidemiology and emphasize the importance of surveillance and targeted interventions.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the long-term epidemiological characteristics and pathogen spectrum changes of other infectious diarrhea (OID) in Kunming, China, from 2011 to 2025, as OID is one of the most frequently reported notifiable infectious diseases in China.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Kunming, China, from 2011 to 2025, focusing on OID cases across all age groups, with a particular emphasis on children aged 0-4 years. It included 152,090 OID cases reported during the surveillance period.
elements_en.methods: Temporal, spatial, demographic and pathogen-related patterns were assessed using descriptive epidemiological analyses, time-series and trend analyses. Joinpoint regression was performed to assess long-term incidence trends across different population groups. Seasonal-trend decomposition using Loess (STL) and continuous wavelet transform were applied to identify periodic fluctuations and temporal changes in epidemic patterns. The Shannon-Wiener diversity index was used to evaluate changes in pathogen diversity.
elements_en.main_results: From 2011 to 2025, Kunming reported 152,090 OID cases, with a mean annual incidence of 134.3 per 100,000 population (range: 62.7-273.2 per 100,000). Incidence increased significantly over the surveillance period (AAPC = 11.2%, 95% CI 3.5 to 19.3), showing a marked acceleration after 2023. OID cases occurred across all age groups, with those aged 0-4 years accounting for the largest proportion (67.0%, 101,899/152,090), while incidence increased across all age groups (all P < 0.001).
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that OID epidemiology in Kunming has shifted from traditional epidemic fluctuations toward broader structural changes, characterized by expanding affected populations, evolving pathogen composition, and changing spatial epidemic patterns.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the increasing epidemiological complexity of OID and the need for prevention strategies that integrate population diversity, spatial differences, and pathogen composition to address emerging control challenges.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The observed changes in pathogen composition may have been influenced by testing practices, which limits the confidence in the findings. However, the study provides a comprehensive analysis of OID trends and patterns, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨2011年至2025年中国昆明市其他传染病性腹泻(OID)的长期流行病学特征及病原谱变化,因为OID是中国最常见的法定传染病之一。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在中国昆明市进行,时间跨度为2011年至2025年,重点关注所有年龄段的OID病例,特别是0-4岁儿童。研究包括了研究期间报告的152,090例OID病例。
elements_zh.methods: 通过描述性流行病学分析、时间序列和趋势分析,评估了时间、空间、人口学和病原相关模式。使用Joinpoint回归分析来评估不同人口群体中OID发病率的长期趋势。局部回归季节趋势分解(STL)和连续小波变换被用于识别疫情模式中的周期性波动和时间变化。香农-维纳多样性指数用于评估病原体多样性的变化。
elements_zh.main_results: From 2011 to 2025, Kunming reported 152,090 OID cases, with a mean annual incidence of 134.3 per 100,000 population (range: 62.7-273.2 per 100,000). Incidence increased significantly over the surveillance period (AAPC = 11.2%, 95% CI 3.5 to 19.3), showing a marked acceleration after 2023. OID cases occurred across all age groups, with those aged 0-4 years accounting for the largest proportion (67.0%, 101,899/152,090), while incidence increased across all age groups (all P < 0.001).
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,昆明市OID的流行趋势已从传统的疫情波动转向更广泛的结构性变化,表现为受影响人群的扩大、病原体构成的演变以及空间疫情模式的变化。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果突显了OID流行病学复杂性的增加,并强调需要制定综合考虑人口多样性、空间差异和病原体构成的预防策略,以应对新兴的防控挑战。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 观察到的病原体构成变化可能受到检测实践的影响,这限制了研究结果的可信度。然而,本研究提供了OID趋势和模式的全面分析,支持中等程度的可信度评估。

papers.title_zh: 2011年至2025年中国昆明市其他传染病性腹泻的时空动态及病原谱分析
papers.source_body_en: Other infectious diarrhea (OID) is one of the most frequently reported notifiable infectious diseases in China. As the capital of Yunnan Province, Kunming serves as an important regional hub in Southwest China and a gateway to the Greater Mekong Subregion. Its patterns of regional population mobility and local disease transmission are complex and region-specific, making Kunming an informative setting for sentinel surveillance and epidemiological investigations. This study investigated the long-term epidemiological characteristics and pathogen spectrum changes of OID in Kunming from 2011 to 2025. Temporal, spatial, demographic and pathogen-related patterns were assessed using descriptive epidemiological analyses, time-series and trend analyses. Seasonal-trend decomposition using Loess (STL) was utilized to characterize long-term temporal trends and seasonal patterns of OID. Continuous wavelet transform was applied to identify periodic fluctuations and temporal changes in epidemic patterns. The Shannon-Wiener diversity index was used to evaluate changes in pathogen diversity. Joinpoint regression was performed to assess long-term incidence trends across different population groups. From 2011 to 2025, Kunming reported 152,090 OID cases, with a mean annual incidence of 134.3 per 100,000 population (range: 62.7-273.2 per 100,000). Incidence increased significantly over the surveillance period (AAPC = 11.2%, 95% CI 3.5 to 19.3), showing a marked acceleration after 2023. OID cases occurred across all age groups, with those aged 0-4 years accounting for the largest proportion (67.0%, 101,899/152,090), while incidence increased across all age groups (all P < 0.001). Among 38,902 laboratory-confirmed cases, viral infections predominated (99.2%). Rotavirus remained the most prevalent pathogen (69.7%), followed by norovirus (26.7%). Both were mainly concentrated among children aged 0-4 years (89.1% and 72.0%, respectively). Spatially, OID incidence varied across counties and districts, with increasingly synchronized regional increases observed in recent years, particularly after 2024. Our findings from routinely collected surveillance data indicate that OID epidemiology in Kunming has shifted from traditional epidemic fluctuations toward broader structural changes, characterized by expanding affected populations, evolving pathogen composition, and changing spatial epidemic patterns. Although the observed changes in pathogen composition may have been influenced by testing practices, the findings highlight increasing epidemiological complexity and emerging control challenges. Accordingly, prevention strategies should integrate population diversity, spatial differences, and pathogen composition.

papers.title: Visual Detection of Foodborne Viruses in Leafy Greens Using an AsCas12f-Split-G-Quadruplex Sensor.
papers.abstract: Abstract Foodborne viruses are responsible for a substantial burden of disease worldwide, with fresh produce serving as the most abundant vehicle for transmission. However, rapid detection in solid produce, such as leafy greens, remains underdeveloped, as conventional methods often require labor-intensive sample preparation and specialized instrumentation. Herein, we present a colorimetric CRISPR-split-G4 biosensor for rapid viral surveillance in leafy greens that combines reverse transcription recombinase polymerase amplification (RT-RPA), AsCas12f-mediated trans-cleavage, and a modular split-G-quadruplex (split-G4) reporter system. In this system, target recognition activates the trans-cleavage activity of AsCas12f, resulting in degradation of a blocker strand and subsequent assembly of a catalytically active G4-hemin DNAzyme that generates a visible signal easily detectable by the naked eye. Using norovirus as a model pathogen, the platform exhibited high analytical sensitivity and specificity, enabling reliable detection of viral particles with minimal instrumentation. To evaluate practical applicability, the assay was coupled with a simplified leaf-disk extraction workflow and successfully applied to contaminated romaine lettuce and baby spinach samples without requiring viral nucleic acid purification. The platform achieved detection limits of 1000 and 5000 viral copies per 100 mg of romaine lettuce and spinach tissue, respectively. From sample processing to visual readout, the entire assay was completed in approximately 2 h. By integrating isothermal amplification, CRISPR-based target recognition, and instrument-free signal generation into a streamlined workflow, this strategy provides a promising platform for decentralized food safety monitoring and establishes a flexible framework for the on-site detection of viral pathogens in complex food matrices.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 食源性病毒在全球范围内导致了显著的疾病负担,其中新鲜农产品是传播病毒传播的主要媒介。然而,对于固体农产品(如叶类蔬菜)的快速检测仍处于发展阶段,因为传统方法通常需要繁琐的样品制备和专门的仪器。本文中,我们提出了一种基于颜色变化的CRISPR-拆分G4生物传感器,用于叶类蔬菜中监测病毒的快速检测,该传感器结合了逆转录重组酶聚合酶扩增(RT-RPA)、AsCas12f介导的转切割作用以及模块化的拆分G-四联体(split-G4)报告系统。在该系统中,目标识别激活了AsCas12f的转切割活性,导致阻断链的降解,并随后组装出具有催化活性的G4-血红素DNA酶,从而产生肉眼可见的信号。以诺如病毒作为模型病原体,该平台表现出高分析灵敏度和特异性,能够在最少仪器条件下可靠地检测病毒颗粒。为了评估实际应用性,该检测方法与简化后的叶盘提取流程相结合,并成功应用于未经过病毒核酸纯化的受污染生菜和婴儿菠菜样本。该平台在生菜和菠菜组织中分别实现了每100毫克1000和5000个病毒拷贝的检测限。从样品处理到肉眼读数,整个检测过程大约需要2小时。通过将等温扩增、基于CRISPR的目标识别以及无需仪器的信号生成整合到一个优化的工作流程中,该策略为分散式食品安全监测提供了有前景的平台,并为在复杂食品基质中现场检测病毒病原体建立了一个灵活的框架。

analysis.event: The FDA cleared an updated bioMérieux GI Panels with a redesigned Norovirus assay, as reported by Clinical Lab Products.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The update is a diagnostic improvement and does not report any cases, deaths, or exposures related to norovirus outbreaks. It focuses on enhancing testing capabilities.

analysis.brief_en: The FDA has cleared an updated bioMérieux GI Panels with a redesigned Norovirus assay, enhancing diagnostic capabilities for gastrointestinal infections. This update, reported by Clinical Lab Products on November 9, 2026, was effective from November 2, 2026, and aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of testing for human norovirus. The change does not indicate any new outbreaks or cases but reflects advancements in diagnostic technology. The event is confirmed as a regulatory approval, with no reported cases, deaths, or exposures linked to the norovirus in this context. The update is part of broader efforts to refine diagnostic tools for infectious diseases, including norovirus gastroenteritis, without introducing new public health risks.

news.content_zh: FDA批准了更新的bioMérieux胃肠病原体检测面板,采用重新设计的诺如病毒检测方法,以增强对胃肠感染的诊断能力。该更新由Clinical Lab Products于2026年11月9日报道,自2026年11月2日起生效,旨在提高对人类诺如病毒的检测准确性和效率。此次变更并不表示出现了新的暴发病例或情况,而是反映了诊断技术的进步。该事件被确认为监管批准,且在此上下文中未报告与诺如病毒相关的病例、死亡或暴露事件。此次更新是更大范围努力的一部分,旨在改进传染病诊断工具,包括诺如病毒引起的胃肠炎,而不引入新的公共卫生风险。

analysis.time: US poised to lose measles elimination status—what does that mean?
analysis.event: Norovirus is identified as the primary cause of cruise ship outbreaks over the past 30 years, though other pathogens are increasingly contributing. This is reported by CIDRAP.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Norovirus has been the main cause of outbreaks on cruise ships, but other pathogens are gaining prominence. The article notes that the US is at risk of losing measles elimination status, which could be related to broader public health concerns.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: CIDRAP has published the report, and the article discusses ongoing public health threats and the need for vaccination. The status of measles elimination in the US is under consideration by an international body.

analysis.brief_en: The article from CIDRAP, published on November 9, 2026, highlights that norovirus has been the primary cause of cruise ship outbreaks for the past 30 years. However, it also notes that other pathogens are increasingly contributing to such outbreaks. The report underscores broader public health concerns, including the potential for the US to lose its measles elimination status. An international body is currently evaluating evidence suggesting measles is becoming endemic again. While norovirus remains a significant issue, the article also touches on other health threats, such as drug-resistant infections and long-term effects of dental procedures. The piece serves as a reminder of the importance of vaccination and public health preparedness, especially for vulnerable populations like children and adults with weakened immunity. The findings are based on CIDRAP's analysis and are part of a larger discussion on infectious disease trends and responses.

news.title_zh: Norovirus No. 1 cause of cruise ship outbreaks for past 30 years, but other pathogens gaining - CIDRAP
news.source_body_en: The article from CIDRAP, published on November 9, 2026, highlights that norovirus has been the primary cause of cruise ship outbreaks for the past 30 years. However, it also notes that other pathogens are increasingly contributing to such outbreaks. The report underscores broader public health concerns, including the potential for the US to lose its measles elimination status. An international body is currently evaluating evidence suggesting measles is becoming endemic again. While norovirus remains a significant issue, the article also touches on other health threats, such as drug-resistant infections and long-term effects of dental procedures. The piece serves as a reminder of the importance of vaccination and public health preparedness, especially for vulnerable populations like children and adults with weakened immunity. The findings are based on CIDRAP's analysis and are part of a larger discussion on infectious disease trends and responses.
news.content_zh: CIDRAP 发布于 2026 年 11 月 9 日的文章指出,诺如病毒 在过去 30 年一直是邮轮 暴发 的主要原因。然而,文章也提到其他病原体正在越来越多地导致此类 暴发。报告强调了更广泛的公共卫生问题,包括美国可能失去麻疹消除状态的潜在风险。一个国际机构目前正在评估麻疹再次成为地方病的证据。尽管 诺如病毒 仍然是一个重要问题,但文章还提及其他健康威胁,例如耐药性感染和牙科手术的长期影响。该文章提醒人们重视 疫苗接种 和公共卫生准备,特别是对儿童和免疫力低下成人等易感人群。这些发现基于 CIDRAP 的分析,并是关于传染病趋势和应对措施的更大讨论的一部分。

news.content_title: Moderna’s norovirus vaccine plans in limbo in wake of phase 3 miss
news.content: Moderna has scrapped plans to enroll a new cohort in a phase 3 trial of its norovirus vaccine and instead will meet with regulators to decide on next steps. The mRNA-focused company launched the late-stage trial of the shot, dubbed mRNA-1403, back in September 2024 as the norovirus season kicked off in the Northern Hemisphere. The trivalent vaccine is designed to prevent the inflammation of the stomach, known as acute gastroenteritis. But Moderna disclosed in July that mRNA-1403 had missed on its interim analysis. At the time, the biopharma's plan was to enroll an additional cohort—but the company appears to have had second thoughts. “Following a review of the program, we have decided not to enroll an additional cohort this coming winter season,” Moderna President Stephen Hoge, M.D., told analysts on a third-quarter earnings call this morning. “Instead, we are engaging with health authorities to determine the next steps for the program.” When pushed by analysts for more details on the norovirus strategy, Hoge promised to “provide further updates following those discussions.” “Once we've had those discussions with them about the potential next steps of the program, we'll be able to provide an update more broadly,” he said on the call. Moderna reported that its R&D expenses had dropped 27% to $583 million in the third quarter, which the company primarily attributed to “lower clinical development costs following the completion and wind-down of certain late-stage studies in the company's infectious disease portfolio, as well as continued cost efficiencies across the organization.” Norovirus, otherwise known as the “stomach bug,” is a very contagious virus that causes inflammation of the stomach and can lead to vomiting and diarrhea, with severe cases potentially leading to hospitalization due to dehydration. Moderna’s mRNA-1403 has hit some roadblocks in the past. In February 2025, the FDA placed it on hold over a reported case of Guillain-Barré syndrome, a neurological disorder where the body’s immune system mistakenly attacks the peripheral nervous system. The following November, the study had to head back for a second season in the Northern Hemisphere after failing to find enough cases down south. Moderna has a clearer route to success for its personalized mRNA cancer vaccine, intismeran autogene . Moderna and its partner Merck & Co. unveiled more data from the vaccine's phase 3 melanoma win in combination with Keytruda at the European Society for Medical Oncology conference last month. The partners are currently working toward regulatory submissions and preparing for a potential commercial launch. “This marked the first combination immunotherapy regimen to demonstrate additional benefit over Keytruda alone in the adjuvant melanoma setting, representing a significant milestone for melanoma patients and their families around the world,” Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel told analysts on the earnings call. Where Big Pharma is placing its bets is one of the hot topics being discussed at Fierce Biotech's high-impact event in London next month. analysis.time: Moderna scrapped plans to enroll a new cohort in a phase 3 trial of its norovirus vaccine in the coming winter season, as reported in the third-quarter earnings call on 2026-11-06. The phase 3 trial was launched in September 2024, and the interim analysis was disclosed in July 2024.
analysis.location_and_population: The trial was initially planned for the Northern Hemisphere, with the vaccine targeting human norovirus and preventing acute gastroenteritis, which affects humans, particularly in settings where norovirus is prevalent.
analysis.event: Moderna's phase 3 trial for its norovirus vaccine, mRNA-1403, was paused due to an interim analysis miss, and the company decided not to enroll an additional cohort this winter. The company is now engaging with health authorities to determine next steps.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The trial's failure to meet its interim analysis goals may impact the development timeline of the vaccine. However, no specific case counts, death counts, or exposure numbers were reported in the supplied evidence. The risk to public health is not explicitly stated.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Moderna is in discussions with health authorities to determine the next steps for the program. The company has not provided further details on the norovirus strategy, and the outcome of these discussions remains uncertain.

analysis.brief_en: Moderna has paused its plans to enroll a new cohort in the phase 3 trial of its norovirus vaccine, mRNA-1403, following an interim analysis miss in July 2024. The trial, launched in September 2024 in the Northern Hemisphere, was intended to prevent acute gastroenteritis caused by human norovirus. Instead of proceeding with the trial this winter, the company will meet with regulators to decide on future actions. Moderna's President, Stephen Hoge, stated that the decision was based on a review of the program and that further updates will be provided after these discussions. The vaccine's development has faced challenges, including an FDA hold in February 2025 due to a reported case of Guillain-Barré syndrome. While the company has a clearer path for its personalized mRNA cancer vaccine, the norovirus vaccine's progress remains uncertain. news.title: FDA Clears Updated bioMérieux GI Panels With Redesigned Norovirus Assay
news.rss_summary_html: FDA clears bioMérieux’s updated GI panels with redesigned norovirus assay and improved Campylobacter detection.
news.excerpt_original: FDA clears bioMérieux’s updated GI panels with redesigned norovirus assay and improved Campylobacter detection.

news.content_title: FDA Clears bioMérieux Gastrointestinal Panels With Norovirus Update
news.content: Diagnostic Technologies Anatomic Pathology Clinical Chemistry Digital Pathology Flow Cytometry Hematology & Serology Immunoassay Mass Spectrometry Microbiology Molecular Diagnostics Point-of-Care Urinalysis & Toxicology Lab Products Biochemicals & Chemical Reagents Information Technology Lab Automation Lab Equipment Lab Safety Labware & Consumables Quality Systems Disease States Allergy & Autoimmune Cancer Cardiovascular Cerebrovascular Dementias & Alzheimer’s Diabetes & Metabolic Diseases Infectious Diseases Kidney Disease Respiratory Disease Sepsis Womens Health Lab Management Accreditation Company News Compliance Proficiency Testing Resource Center Resources Podcasts Webcasts White Papers Videos Comparison Guides Edition Archive Select Page FDA Clears Updated bioMérieux GI Panels With Redesigned Norovirus Assay Nov 9, 2026 | Gastrointestinal Infections | The molecular panels feature changes to norovirus and Campylobacter detection intended to improve specificity, with results available in about one hour. bioMérieux has received US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 510(k) clearance for the BIOFIRE FILMARRAY Gastrointestinal 1.1 (GI1.1) Panel and the BIOFIRE FILMARRAY GI1.1 Panel Mid, the company announced. The GI1.1 Panel also has been CE marked under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation, which enables commercialization across European markets. The molecular panels test for 22 and 11 of the most common bacteria, viruses, and parasites associated with gastroenteritis, respectively, from a single sample, with results in about one hour. What Changed in the New Versions According to the company, the new versions include a redesigned norovirus GI/GII assay and a software-based improvement for Campylobacter detection. bioMérieux says the changes further strengthen the panels’ specificity. The panels detect pathogens directly from stool samples of individuals with signs or symptoms of gastrointestinal infection. They are designed for use on the BIOFIRE FILMARRAY 2.0 and TORCH systems, require about two minutes of hands-on time for setup, and have a run time of about one hour. The GI1.1 Panel targets bacteria including Campylobacter, Clostridioides difficile, Salmonella, and Shigella/enteroinvasive E. coli; viruses including adenovirus F40/41, norovirus GI/GII, and rotavirus A; and parasites including Cryptosporidium, Cyclospora cayetanensis, and Giardia lamblia. The GI1.1 Panel Mid covers a smaller set that includes norovirus GI/GII, Campylobacter, C difficile toxin A/B, Salmonella, and Cryptosporidium. Clinical and Public Health Context Symptoms of acute infectious gastroenteritis, such as diarrhea, vomiting, fever, and abdominal pain, are often nonspecific, which makes diagnostic testing more critical. The highest disease burden falls on young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. The World Health Organization estimates that diarrheal diseases cause 1.7 billion cases worldwide each year and remain among the leading causes of death in children younger than 60 months. “This is particularly important for norovirus, which remains one of the most prevalent and disruptive causes of acute gastroenteritis, and can spread rapidly in communities and healthcare settings. By providing timely and reliable diagnostic information, these panels can help clinicians make informed decisions earlier, support infection control efforts, and ultimately improve the patient experience,” says Charles K. Cooper, executive vice president and chief medical officer of bioMérieux, in a release. Jennifer Zinn, executive vice president of clinical operations at bioMérieux, says the company drew on post-market surveillance and research and development advances to develop the latest generation of the panels. “As the global leader in gastrointestinal syndromic testing, we leveraged robust post-market surveillance and R&D advancements to develop the latest generation of our BIOFIRE FILMARRAY Gastrointestinal Panels. By providing rapid, actionable results, we support better clinical decision-making for improved patient management and deliver greater value to laboratories and clinicians when it matters most,” says Zinn, in a release. The GI1.1 Panel will be deployed across all regions, while the GI1.1 Panel Mid will initially be available in the United States. news.content_original: Diagnostic Technologies Anatomic Pathology Clinical Chemistry Digital Pathology Flow Cytometry Hematology & Serology Immunoassay Mass Spectrometry Microbiology Molecular Diagnostics Point-of-Care Urinalysis & Toxicology Lab Products Biochemicals & Chemical Reagents Information Technology Lab Automation Lab Equipment Lab Safety Labware & Consumables Quality Systems Disease States Allergy & Autoimmune Cancer Cardiovascular Cerebrovascular Dementias & Alzheimer’s Diabetes & Metabolic Diseases Infectious Diseases Kidney Disease Respiratory Disease Sepsis Womens Health Lab Management Accreditation Company News Compliance Proficiency Testing Resource Center Resources Podcasts Webcasts White Papers Videos Comparison Guides Edition Archive Select Page FDA Clears Updated bioMérieux GI Panels With Redesigned Norovirus Assay Nov 9, 2026 | Gastrointestinal Infections | The molecular panels feature changes to norovirus and Campylobacter detection intended to improve specificity, with results available in about one hour. bioMérieux has received US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 510(k) clearance for the BIOFIRE FILMARRAY Gastrointestinal 1.1 (GI1.1) Panel and the BIOFIRE FILMARRAY GI1.1 Panel Mid, the company announced. The GI1.1 Panel also has been CE marked under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation, which enables commercialization across European markets. The molecular panels test for 22 and 11 of the most common bacteria, viruses, and parasites associated with gastroenteritis, respectively, from a single sample, with results in about one hour. What Changed in the New Versions According to the company, the new versions include a redesigned norovirus GI/GII assay and a software-based improvement for Campylobacter detection. bioMérieux says the changes further strengthen the panels’ specificity. The panels detect pathogens directly from stool samples of individuals with signs or symptoms of gastrointestinal infection. They are designed for use on the BIOFIRE FILMARRAY 2.0 and TORCH systems, require about two minutes of hands-on time for setup, and have a run time of about one hour. The GI1.1 Panel targets bacteria including Campylobacter, Clostridioides difficile, Salmonella, and Shigella/enteroinvasive E. coli; viruses including adenovirus F40/41, norovirus GI/GII, and rotavirus A; and parasites including Cryptosporidium, Cyclospora cayetanensis, and Giardia lamblia. The GI1.1 Panel Mid covers a smaller set that includes norovirus GI/GII, Campylobacter, C difficile toxin A/B, Salmonella, and Cryptosporidium. Clinical and Public Health Context Symptoms of acute infectious gastroenteritis, such as diarrhea, vomiting, fever, and abdominal pain, are often nonspecific, which makes diagnostic testing more critical. The highest disease burden falls on young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. The World Health Organization estimates that diarrheal diseases cause 1.7 billion cases worldwide each year and remain among the leading causes of death in children younger than 60 months. “This is particularly important for norovirus, which remains one of the most prevalent and disruptive causes of acute gastroenteritis, and can spread rapidly in communities and healthcare settings. By providing timely and reliable diagnostic information, these panels can help clinicians make informed decisions earlier, support infection control efforts, and ultimately improve the patient experience,” says Charles K. Cooper, executive vice president and chief medical officer of bioMérieux, in a release. Jennifer Zinn, executive vice president of clinical operations at bioMérieux, says the company drew on post-market surveillance and research and development advances to develop the latest generation of the panels. “As the global leader in gastrointestinal syndromic testing, we leveraged robust post-market surveillance and R&D advancements to develop the latest generation of our BIOFIRE FILMARRAY Gastrointestinal Panels. By providing rapid, actionable results, we support better clinical decision-making for improved patient management and deliver greater value to laboratories and clinicians when it matters most,” says Zinn, in a release. The GI1.1 Panel will be deployed across all regions, while the GI1.1 Panel Mid will initially be available in the United States. news.title_original: FDA Clears Updated bioMérieux GI Panels With Redesigned Norovirus Assay

analysis.time: The FDA cleared the updated bioMérieux GI Panels with a redesigned Norovirus assay on Nov 9, 2026. The changes were based on post-market surveillance and R&D advancements, with the new versions being deployed globally.
analysis.location_and_population: The updated panels are available for use in the United States and across European markets. They are designed for testing stool samples from individuals with signs or symptoms of gastrointestinal infection, including young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals.
analysis.event: The FDA granted 510(k) clearance for the updated bioMérieux GI Panels, which include a redesigned Norovirus GI/GII assay. The panels are intended to improve diagnostic specificity for gastrointestinal infections.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The panels test for 22 common bacteria, viruses, and parasites associated with gastroenteritis, including Norovirus GI/GII, from a single sample. They are designed to provide rapid, actionable results to support clinical decision-making and infection control efforts.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The panels are now available for deployment globally, with the GI1.1 Panel Mid initially available in the United States. The changes aim to strengthen diagnostic specificity, and the company claims these updates will improve patient management and laboratory value.

analysis.brief_en: The FDA has cleared updated bioMérieux GI Panels with a redesigned Norovirus GI/GII assay, effective Nov 9, 2026. These panels are intended to improve diagnostic specificity for gastrointestinal infections, including Norovirus, by testing for 22 common pathogens from a single stool sample. The new versions are designed for use on the BIOFIRE FILMARRAY 2.0 and TORCH systems, with results available in about one hour. The GI1.1 Panel will be deployed globally, while the GI1.1 Panel Mid will initially be available in the United States. The changes were based on post-market surveillance and R&D advancements, and the company claims they will support better clinical decision-making and infection control efforts. The panels are relevant for diagnosing Norovirus gastroenteritis, which is a significant cause of acute gastroenteritis, particularly in vulnerable populations such as young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals.

By Jongho, Jang Published 2026-11-06 11:59 Share this article X Facebook Copy Copy URL copied. AI-generated image [Sportschosun reporter Jang Jong-ho] As the weather turns colder, special caution is warranted against norovirus gastroenteritis, which commonly affects infants and young children. Norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastrointestinal infection in winter and circulates from November through the following spring. It spreads particularly quickly among young children in group settings such as daycare centers and kindergartens. Unlike adults, infants and young children are prone to developing sudden vomiting as an initial symptom and face a greater risk of dehydration, making prompt early care and good hygiene essential. According to past surveillance data from the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency, sentinel surveillance at 210 hospital-level medical institutions nationwide found that norovirus infections began to increase in the first week of November 2025, and the weekly number of cases reached 617 in the third week of January 2026. Notably, infants and young children aged 0 to 6 accounted for 51.1% of all cases at the time, underscoring the importance of preventing infections and maintaining good hygiene among young children in winter. Norovirus causes symptoms such as vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain after an incubation period of 12 to 48 hours. Diarrhea is often more prominent in adults, while sudden, repeated vomiting can be a main symptom in children. Therefore, even if there is no diarrhea, norovirus gastroenteritis should be considered if a child suddenly vomits several times. It is not advisable to automatically withhold food from a child who is vomiting. If the child is breastfed, continue breastfeeding; if the vomiting is severe, offering small amounts of oral rehydration solution frequently can help. Once the vomiting subsides and the child is able to eat, it is best to offer small portions of the foods they usually eat. The main concern with norovirus gastroenteritis is dehydration. Infants and young children can lose body fluids rapidly through repeated vomiting and diarrhea, and may become dehydrated more easily than adults. If a child keeps vomiting even when given small amounts of water or rehydration solution, or has noticeably less urine and seems less energetic than usual, dehydration may be developing. In such cases, seek medical care promptly. Norovirus is highly contagious and can cause infection from even a small amount of the virus. It spreads not only through contaminated food or water, but also through an infected person’s vomit or stool and through hands or toys contaminated with the virus. In particular, if a child’s surroundings become contaminated when they vomit, the virus can remain on surfaces for a long time and spread to family members or other children at daycare. To prevent infection, it is important to wash hands thoroughly with soap and running water for at least 30 seconds rather than relying solely on alcohol-based hand sanitizer. Food should be cooked thoroughly, and areas where a child has vomited or had diarrhea should be cleaned and disinfected with a product effective against norovirus. Because the virus may continue to be shed for a period after symptoms improve, children should stay home from daycare for at least 48 hours after vomiting and diarrhea have completely stopped. Baek Jeong-hyeon, a pediatrician at Woori Children’s Hospital, said, “It is important to know how many times a child has vomited, but it is even more important to check whether the child can take in and keep down even small amounts of fluid, whether their urine output has decreased, and whether they seem less energetic than usual.” The specialist urged, “Dehydration can progress quickly, especially in very young children. SelectScience CLINICAL24 2026 Home /News NewsClinical Diagnostics BIOFIRE FILMARRAY GI1.1 Panels receive FDA clearance for gastrointestinal pathogen detection bioMérieux Updated 22- and 11-target PCR panels feature a redesigned norovirus GI/GII assay and improved Campylobacter detection 9 Nov 2026 Summary: bioMérieux announces U.S. FDA 510(k) clearance for the BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI1.1 Panel and GI1.1 Panel Mid. The panels detect 22 and 11 gastrointestinal pathogens, respectively, from a single stool sample, with results in about one hour. Both feature a redesigned norovirus GI/GII assay and a software-based improvement for Campylobacter detection. The GI1.1 Panel also has IVDR CE marking for European commercialization; the Panel Mid will initially be available in the United States. bioMérieux, a world leader in the field of in vitro diagnostics, today announces that the BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® Gastrointestinal 1.1 (GI1.1) Panel has obtained U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 510(k) clearance and IVDR1 CE marking, and the BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® Gastrointestinal 1.1 (GI1.1) Panel Mid has received U.S. FDA 510(k) clearance. These PCR* molecular panels test 22 and 11, respectively, of the most common bacteria, viruses, and parasites associated with gastroenteritis, all from one sample, with results available in about one hour. Acute infectious gastroenteritis remains a significant global health concern, driven by a diverse and continually evolving range of viral, bacterial, and parasitic pathogens that inflame the gastrointestinal tract. Clinical manifestations such as diarrhea, vomiting, fever, and abdominal pain are often nonspecific, making diagnostic testing even more critical. The highest disease burden affects young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Diarrheal diseases, which cause an estimated 1.7 billion cases worldwide each year,2 continue to rank among the leading causes of mortality in children under 60 months of age. As pathogen populations shift over time through genetic variation, emergence of new strains, and changes in epidemiological patterns, diagnostic technologies must evolve to ensure accurate detection, timely clinical decision-making, and effective public health responses. Redesigned norovirus assay and improved Campylobacter detection In line with its commitment to continuous improvements and to delivering high-quality diagnostic solutions, bioMérieux has developed the BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI1.1 Panel and BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI1.1 Panel Mid. These new versions include a redesigned norovirus GI/GII assay and a software-based improvement for Campylobacter detection, further strengthening the panels’ specificity and providing greater confidence in every result. These molecular syndromic testing solutions are capable of simultaneously detecting 22 and 11 pathogens*, respectively, directly from stool samples of individuals presenting with signs and/or symptoms of gastrointestinal infection. Designed for use on bioMérieux’s BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® 2.0 and TORCH systems, they require about two minutes of hands-on time for setup, with an approximate run time of about one hour. Helping clinicians make informed decisions “The regulatory authorizations of these enhanced gastrointestinal panels mark an important milestone in ensuring healthcare providers have access to the most up-to-date diagnostic tools to support patient care. This is particularly important for norovirus, which remains one of the most prevalent and disruptive causes of acute gastroenteritis, and can spread rapidly in communities and healthcare settings. By providing timely and reliable diagnostic information, these panels can help clinicians make informed decisions earlier, support infection control efforts, and ultimately improve the patient experience,” declared Dr. Charles K. Cooper, Executive Vice President, Chief Medical Officer, bioMérieux. “At bioMérieux, innovation extends beyond developing new diagnostic solutions. It includes continuously enhancing the performance of technologies within our trusted portfolio used by healthcare professionals every day. As the global leader in gastrointestinal syndromic testing, we leveraged robust post-market surveillance and R&D advancements to develop the latest generation of our BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® Gastrointestinal Panels. By providing rapid, actionable results, we support better clinical decision-making for improved patient management and deliver greater value to laboratories and clinicians when it matters most,” commented Jennifer Zinn, Executive Vice President, Clinical Operations, bioMérieux. A global commercialization strategy The BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI1.1 Panel will be deployed across all regions, while the BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI1.1 Panel Mid will be initially available in the United States. In addition to receiving U.S. FDA 510(k) clearance, the BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI1.1 Panel has also been CE marked under the IVDR,1 enabling commercialization across European markets. * BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI 1.1 Panel: Bacteria: Campylobacter (C. jejuni/C. coli/C. upsaliensis), Clostridioides (Clostridium) difficile (toxin A/B), Plesiomonas shigelloides, Salmonella, Vibrio (V. parahaemolyticus/V. vulnificus/V. cholerae), Vibrio cholerae, Yersinia enterocolitica, Enteroaggregative E. coli (EAEC), Enteropathogenic E. coli (EPEC), Enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC) lt/st, Shiga-like toxin-producing E. coli (STEC) stx1/stx2, Shigella/Enteroinvasive E. coli (EIEC) Viruses: Adenovirus F40/41, Astrovirus, Norovirus GI/GII, Rotavirus A, Sapovirus (I, II, IV, and V) Parasites: Cryptosporidium, Cyclospora cayetanensis, Entamoeba histolytica, Giardia lamblia BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI 1.1 Panel Mid: Bacteria: Campylobacter (C. jejuni/C. coli/C. upsaliensis), Clostridioides (Clostridium) difficile (toxin A/B), Salmonella, Vibrio (V. parahaemolyticus/V. vulnificus/V. cholerae), Yersinia enterocolitica, Shiga-like toxin-producing E. coli (STEC) stx1/stx2, Shigella/Enteroinvasive E. coli (EIEC). panels feature a redesigned norovirus GI/GII assay and improved Campylobacter detection 9 Nov 2026 Summary: bioMérieux announces U.S. FDA 510(k) clearance for the BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI1.1 Panel and GI1.1 Panel Mid. The panels detect 22 and 11 gastrointestinal pathogens, respectively, from a single stool sample, with results in about one hour. Both feature a redesigned norovirus GI/GII assay and a software-based improvement for Campylobacter detection. The GI1.1 Panel also has IVDR CE marking for European commercialization; the Panel Mid will initially be available in the United States. bioMérieux, a world leader in the field of in vitro diagnostics, today announces that the BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® Gastrointestinal 1.1 (GI1.1) Panel has obtained U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 510(k) clearance and IVDR1 CE marking, and the BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® Gastrointestinal 1.1 (GI1.1) Panel Mid has received U.S. FDA 510(k) clearance. These PCR* molecular panels test 22 and 11, respectively, of the most common bacteria, viruses, and parasites associated with gastroenteritis, all from one sample, with results available in about one hour. Acute infectious gastroenteritis remains a significant global health concern, driven by a diverse and continually evolving range of viral, bacterial, and parasitic pathogens that inflame the gastrointestinal tract. Clinical manifestations such as diarrhea, vomiting, fever, and abdominal pain are often nonspecific, making diagnostic testing even more critical. The highest disease burden affects young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Diarrheal diseases, which cause an estimated 1.7 billion cases worldwide each year,2 continue to rank among the leading causes of mortality in children under 60 months of age. As pathogen populations shift over time through genetic variation, emergence of new strains, and changes in epidemiological patterns, diagnostic technologies must evolve to ensure accurate detection, timely clinical decision-making, and effective public health responses. Redesigned norovirus assay and improved Campylobacter detection In line with its commitment to continuous improvements and to delivering high-quality diagnostic solutions, bioMérieux has developed the BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI1.1 Panel and BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI1.1 Panel Mid. These new versions include a redesigned norovirus GI/GII assay and a software-based improvement for Campylobacter detection, further strengthening the panels’ specificity and providing greater confidence in every result. These molecular syndromic testing solutions are capable of simultaneously detecting 22 and 11 pathogens*, respectively, directly from stool samples of individuals presenting with signs and/or symptoms of gastrointestinal infection. Designed for use on bioMérieux’s BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® 2.0 and TORCH systems, they require about two minutes of hands-on time for setup, with an approximate run time of about one hour. Helping clinicians make informed decisions “The regulatory authorizations of these enhanced gastrointestinal panels mark an important milestone in ensuring healthcare providers have access to the most up-to-date diagnostic tools to support patient care. This is particularly important for norovirus, which remains one of the most prevalent and disruptive causes of acute gastroenteritis, and can spread rapidly in communities and healthcare settings. By providing timely and reliable diagnostic information, these panels can help clinicians make informed decisions earlier, support infection control efforts, and ultimately improve the patient experience,” declared Dr. Charles K. Cooper, Executive Vice President, Chief Medical Officer, bioMérieux. “At bioMérieux, innovation extends beyond developing new diagnostic solutions. It includes continuously enhancing the performance of technologies within our trusted portfolio used by healthcare professionals every day. As the global leader in gastrointestinal syndromic testing, we leveraged robust post-market surveillance and R&D advancements to develop the latest generation of our BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® Gastrointestinal Panels. By providing rapid, actionable results, we support better clinical decision-making for improved patient management and deliver greater value to laboratories and clinicians when it matters most,” commented Jennifer Zinn, Executive Vice President, Clinical Operations, bioMérieux. A global commercialization strategy The BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI1.1 Panel will be deployed across all regions, while the BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI1.1 Panel Mid will be initially available in the United States. In addition to receiving U.S. FDA 510(k) clearance, the BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI1.1 Panel has also been CE marked under the IVDR,1 enabling commercialization across European markets. * BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI 1.1 Panel: Bacteria: Campylobacter (C. jejuni/C. coli/C. upsaliensis), Clostridioides (Clostridium) difficile (toxin A/B), Plesiomonas shigelloides, Salmonella, Vibrio (V. parahaemolyticus/V. vulnificus/V. cholerae), Vibrio cholerae, Yersinia enterocolitica, Enteroaggregative E. coli (EAEC), Enteropathogenic E. coli (EPEC), Enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC) lt/st, Shiga-like toxin-producing E. coli (STEC) stx1/stx2, Shigella/Enteroinvasive E. coli (EIEC) Viruses: Adenovirus F40/41, Astrovirus, Norovirus GI/GII, Rotavirus A, Sapovirus (I, II, IV, and V) Parasites: Cryptosporidium, Cyclospora cayetanensis, Entamoeba histolytica, Giardia lamblia BIOFIRE® FILMARRAY® GI 1.1 Panel Mid: Bacteria: Campylobacter (C. jejuni/C. coli/C. upsaliensis), Clostridioides (Clostridium) difficile (toxin A/B), Salmonella, Vibrio (V. parahaemolyticus/V. vulnificus/V. cholerae), Yersinia enterocolitica, Shiga-like toxin-producing E. coli (STEC) stx1/stx2, Shigella/Enteroinvasive E. coli (EIEC). The company's product pipeline includes norovirus vaccine, a bivalent oral tablet vaccine in Phase 2 clinical trial for the GI.1 and GII.4 norovirus strains; coronavirus vaccine, which is in Phase 2 clinical trial, for the treatment of SARS-CoV-2 infection; seasonal influenza vaccine, which is in Phase 2 clinical trial, to treat H1 influenza infection; and human papillomavirus therapeutic vaccine, which is in preclinical stage, that targets HPV-16 and HPV-18 for cervical cancers and precancerous cervical lesions. CAC 40 : Market closed 8 278,59 pts +0.55% Last updated : 10/11/2026 - 17h35 (last close) Last close data Top performers: ARCELORMITTAL +2,96% ACCOR +2,78% CARREFOUR +2,54% SOCIÉTÉ GÉNÉRALE +2,44% SAFRAN +2,26% Worst performers: STELLANTIS -3,45% DASSAULT SYSTÈMES -1,90% ESSILORLUXOTTICA -1,57% TOTALENERGIES -0,70% L'ORÉAL -0,66% 🏠 Home ➤ Stock news BioMérieux Receives FDA Clearance for Its Revised BioFire Gastrointestinal Panels Announced on 9 November 2026, the clearance covers not a new product but revised versions of the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panels. These versions incorporate a reconfigured test for norovirus GI/GII and optimized algorithms for detecting the Campylobacter bacterium which, according to BioMérieux, enhance the specificity of the tests and the reliability of each result. Published on Nov 09, 2026 at 09:18 Share X LinkedIn Facebook Copy link BIOMERIEUX 91.65 € +0.38 % Add us as a preferred source on Google Two Panels Detecting 22 and 11 Pathogens in About One Hour The BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal 1.1 (GI1.1) Panel and its GI1.1 Panel Mid variant detect respectively 22 and 11 bacteria, viruses and parasites among the most common causes of gastroenteritis, from a single stool sample. Running on the BioFire FilmArray 2.0 and Torch instruments, they require two minutes of preparation for a result in about one hour. The press release recalls that diarrhoeal diseases are among the leading causes of death in children under 60 months of age, with approximately 1.7 billion cases recorded each year worldwide according to the WHO. Since gastroenteritis symptoms are often non-specific, diagnostic tests become, according to the company, all the more essential. Dr Charles K. Cooper, Executive Director of Medical Affairs, highlighted the case of norovirus, which “remains one of the leading causes of acute gastroenteritis worldwide and can spread rapidly within communities and healthcare facilities”. According to him, these tests make it possible to “accelerate clinicians' informed decision-making” and to “support infection control measures”. BioMérieux specified that the GI1.1 Panel will be marketed worldwide, while the GI1.1 Panel Mid will be available primarily in the United States. In addition to the FDA 510(k) clearance, the former has obtained CE marking under the European IVDR regulation on in vitro diagnostic medical devices, enabling its deployment on European markets. Jennifer Zinn, Executive Director of Clinical Operations, placed these updates within an approach of “continuous improvement of the performance of technologies in our portfolio of solutions”. The group relies, she said, “on robust post-market surveillance and on advances from our R&D to continuously evolve” its gastrointestinal tests. CAC 40 : Market closed 8 278,59 pts +0.55% Last updated : 10/11/2026 - 17h35 (last close) Last close data Top performers: ARCELORMITTAL +2,96% ACCOR +2,78% CARREFOUR +2,54% SOCIÉTÉ GÉNÉRALE +2,44% SAFRAN +2,26% Worst performers: STELLANTIS -3,45% DASSAULT SYSTÈMES -1,90% ESSILORLUXOTTICA -1,57% TOTALENERGIES -0,70% L'ORÉAL -0,66% 🏠 Home ➤ Stock news BioMérieux Receives FDA Clearance for Its Revised BioFire Gastrointestinal Panels Announced on 9 November 2026, the clearance covers not a new product but revised versions of the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panels. These versions incorporate a reconfigured test for norovirus GI/GII and optimized algorithms for detecting the Campylobacter bacterium which, according to BioMérieux, enhance the specificity of the tests and the reliability of each result. Published on Nov 09, 2026 at 09:18 Share X LinkedIn Facebook Copy link BIOMERIEUX 91.65 € +0.38 % Add us as a preferred source on Google Two Panels Detecting 22 and 11 Pathogens in About One Hour The BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal 1.1 (GI1.1) Panel and its GI1.1 Panel Mid variant detect respectively 22 and 11 bacteria, viruses and parasites among the most common causes of gastroenteritis, from a single stool sample. Running on the BioFire FilmArray 2.0 and Torch instruments, they require two minutes of preparation for a result in about one hour. The press release recalls that diarrhoeal diseases are among the leading causes of death in children under 60 months of age, with approximately 1.7 billion cases recorded each year worldwide according to the WHO. Since gastroenteritis symptoms are often non-specific, diagnostic tests become, according to the company, all the more essential. Dr Charles K. Cooper, Executive Director of Medical Affairs, highlighted the case of norovirus, which “remains one of the leading causes of acute gastroenteritis worldwide and can spread rapidly within communities and healthcare facilities”. According to him, these tests make it possible to “accelerate clinicians' informed decision-making” and to “support infection control measures”. BioMérieux specified that the GI1.1 Panel will be marketed worldwide, while the GI1.1 Panel Mid will be available primarily in the United States. In addition to the FDA 510(k) clearance, the former has obtained CE marking under the European IVDR regulation on in vitro diagnostic medical devices, enabling its deployment on European markets. Jennifer Zinn, Executive Director of Clinical Operations, placed these updates within an approach of “continuous improvement of the performance of technologies in our portfolio of solutions”. The group relies, she said, “on robust post-market surveillance and on advances from our R&D to continuously evolve” its gastrointestinal tests. analysis.event: BioMérieux received FDA clearance for its revised BioFire Gastrointestinal Panels, which include updated tests for norovirus GI/GII and optimized algorithms for detecting Campylobacter bacterium. This is a confirmed event reported by BioMérieux.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The revised panels detect 22 and 11 pathogens, enhancing diagnostic reliability. Norovirus remains a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide, capable of rapid spread in communities and healthcare facilities. The event does not report specific case counts or deaths, but emphasizes the importance of diagnostic tests in managing non-specific symptoms.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The FDA clearance and CE marking enable deployment of the GI1.1 Panel globally and the Mid variant in the United States. The company highlights continuous improvement through post-market surveillance and R&D advances. No unresolved information or source limitations are mentioned.

analysis.brief_en: On 9 November 2026, BioMérieux received FDA clearance for its revised BioFire Gastrointestinal Panels, which include updated tests for norovirus GI/GII and optimized algorithms for detecting Campylobacter. These panels are designed to enhance diagnostic specificity and reliability, addressing the challenge of non-specific gastroenteritis symptoms. The GI1.1 Panel will be marketed worldwide, while the Mid variant is primarily available in the United States. The company emphasizes the importance of these updates in supporting infection control and informed clinical decision-making. Norovirus, a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis, is noted for its rapid spread in communities and healthcare settings. The clearance is part of BioMérieux's ongoing commitment to improving diagnostic technologies through post-market surveillance and R&D. No specific case or death counts are reported, but the event underscores the role of advanced testing in managing gastrointestinal diseases.
